newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia GDP seen up 4.9 pct this year - Zagrebacka.
newsitem.headline: Croatia GDP seen up 4.9 pct this year - Zagrebacka.

text.p: Croatia's economic growth could reach 4.9 percent this year and quicken to 5.1 percent in 1998, leading Zagrebacka Banka said on Friday.

Zagrebacka chief economist Zarko Miljenovic said in his quarterly forecast the main spur to growth would come from industry and the tourist trade which is expected to grow by 25 percent in 1997, as more foreign visitors return to Croatia.
"Economic reintegration and revitalisation of Eastern Slavonia will also contribute to a general revival of economic activities in 1997 and next year."
"A positive impact is also expected to come from a gradual recovery of the economy of Bosnia-Herzegovina," Miljenovic said.
He forecast the 1997 nominal gross domestic product (GDP) at 112.7 billion kuna ($18.1 billion), expanding further to 123 billion kuna in 1998.
But the economic recovery was slow in reducing joblessness, now at 16.3 percent officially and expected to rise.
Miljenovic said he expected 1997 industrial output to rise 3.7 percent after a modest 2.8 percent increase last year.
"Data for April and May indicate a gradual revival of the manufacturing industry, especially as regards the production of capital goods," Miljenovic said.
He put it down to rising domestic consumer and investment demand and a recovery of export demand, carried over from 1996. But he warned the consumption boom could harm the economy.
"Domestic aggregate consumption, which is growing faster than GDP this year, will cause the trade gap to widen considerably," he added.
Croatia's trade deficit widened to $3.45 billion between January and May from $3.0 billion in the same year-ago period.

Next year, the main impulse on the demand side is expected to come from private investment and exports, with the growth of personal consumption slowing down considerably, Miljenovic said. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
